domain: family dinner at a Mexican restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a family dinner at a Mexican restaurant by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any changes to the guest list. When the user asks you to evaluate specific menu items, check each item against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to ingredient composition of Mexican dishes, changes in attendance, and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, so my family wants to get together for dinner this Friday at a Mexican place. We haven't all been together in a while — any tips for planning this?

flow_info.value: Four of us going: me, my mom Linda, my brother Jake, and my Uncle Rick
Mom ate some pad thai with peanuts a couple years ago and her throat swelled shut, had to use an EpiPen in the restaurant
Jake got diagnosed with celiac disease last year, he's been really careful about what he eats since then
Uncle Rick has been managing his type 2 diabetes for a few years now, watches what he eats pretty closely
Oh, my cousin Sofia wants to come too — she just told us she's expecting, about 10 weeks along, so exciting
There's a really well-reviewed place called Casa Oaxaca near us, they do traditional Oaxacan food
Jake just texted me, he got called into work for an emergency shift Friday evening. He's bummed about it. He asked if I could bring him back some food though

Uncle Rick just sent a message in the family group chat — his doctor told him at his checkup last week that his blood sugar has been really well controlled, said he doesn't need to restrict his diet anymore as long as he keeps up his medication

I looked at Casa Oaxaca's menu online. They have a set family dinner option: chicken mole poblano, cheese enchiladas in flour tortillas, carne asada tacos on corn tortillas, fish ceviche, guacamole with tortilla chips, and tres leches cake for dessert. How does that look for us?

constraints.value: Cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived ingredients
constraints.surface_form: Mom ate some pad thai with peanuts a couple years ago and her throat swelled shut, we had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Throat swelling + EpiPen use → severe allergic reaction
Reaction triggered by peanuts in pad thai → peanut allergy
Peanut allergy → must avoid all peanut and peanut-derived ingredients

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten or gluten-containing ingredients including wheat flour
constraints.surface_form: Jake got diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease diagnosis → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
Must avoid all gluten-containing foods including wheat flour tortillas

constraints.value: Needs to limit sugar and refined carbohydrate intake due to type 2 diabetes
constraints.surface_form: Uncle Rick has been managing his type 2 diabetes for a few years now, watches what he eats pretty closely
inference_chain: Blood sugar management → limit sugar and refined carbs

constraints.value: Should avoid raw or undercooked fish and seafood due to pregnancy
constraints.surface_form: My cousin Sofia just told us she's expecting, about 10 weeks along
inference_chain: Expecting / 10 weeks along → pregnant, first trimester
Pregnancy food safety → avoid raw fish, undercooked seafood, certain cheeses

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a family dinner at a Mexican restaurant. You will introduce your mom Linda, brother Jake, Uncle Rick, and later cousin Sofia. Mom had a severe peanut reaction (EpiPen), Jake has celiac, Uncle Rick has diabetes. Sofia joins later and is pregnant. Jake will have to cancel but wants takeaway. Uncle Rick's doctor will clear his diet restriction. At the end you will share a specific menu and ask how it looks — you must NOT hint at any specific dietary problems or tell the assistant what to check for.

You are a warm, easygoing family organizer. You always refer to family members by name or relation in third person (e.g. 'Mom told me...', 'Jake texted me...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change — family stuff is always a bit chaotic and you roll with it. You keep things casual and upbeat.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for family member updates

aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies chicken mole poblano as problematic for Mom (mole contains ground peanuts), cheese enchiladas in flour tortillas as problematic for Jake's takeaway (gluten), fish ceviche as problematic for Sofia (pregnant, raw fish). Agent notes scope distinction for enchiladas (fine for table, not for Jake's takeaway).
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 menu items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Three items have problems. Chicken mole poblano: traditional mole poblano sauce contains ground peanuts as a key ingredient — this is dangerous for Mom Linda who has a severe peanut allergy (anaphylaxis, required EpiPen). Fish ceviche: ceviche is raw fish cured in citrus, not cooked — Sofia is pregnant (first trimester) and should avoid raw fish. Cheese enchiladas in flour tortillas: flour tortillas contain wheat gluten — fine for everyone at the table since Jake is not attending, but CANNOT be packed as takeaway for Jake because of his celiac disease. Carne asada tacos on corn tortillas are fine for everyone including Jake's takeaway (corn tortillas are naturally gluten-free). Guacamole with tortilla chips is fine for everyone. Tres leches cake is fine — Uncle Rick's doctor cleared his diet restriction, so the sugar content is no longer a concern.
required_elements: Chicken mole poblano is problematic: mole sauce contains ground peanuts as a traditional ingredient, which is dangerous for Mom Linda due to her severe peanut allergy
Fish ceviche is problematic: ceviche is raw fish, which Sofia should avoid because she is pregnant
Cheese enchiladas in flour tortillas are fine for the table but must NOT be included in Jake's takeaway because flour tortillas contain gluten and Jake has celiac disease
Carne asada tacos on corn tortillas are safe for everyone at the table and also safe for Jake's takeaway since corn tortillas are gluten-free
Guacamole with tortilla chips is safe for everyone
Uncle Rick no longer has dietary restrictions — his doctor cleared him, so tres leches cake is fine for him
forbidden_elements: Flagging tres leches cake as problematic for Uncle Rick due to sugar or diabetes (his restriction was removed by his doctor)
Saying Jake cannot eat the enchiladas at the table (Jake is not attending dinner, only getting takeaway)
Flagging carne asada tacos as problematic for Jake (corn tortillas are gluten-free)
Over-generalizing Mom's peanut allergy to all nuts or all Mexican food
Ignoring the hidden peanut content in mole poblano and calling chicken mole poblano safe
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking, inferential constraint reasoning, and hidden ingredient knowledge across 9 conversational turns. The primary difficulty mechanism is the hidden ingredient trap: traditional mole poblano sauce contains ground peanuts as a core ingredient, which is not obvious from the dish name. The agent must know this culinary fact to flag the dish for Mom's peanut allergy. Additional tracking challenges: (1) Mom's peanut allergy is delivered as a past event (pad thai incident with EpiPen) requiring inference that she has a peanut allergy, (2) Jake has celiac disease requiring inference that he cannot eat gluten/wheat, (3) Sofia joins late and is pregnant requiring inference about raw fish avoidance, (4) Jake EXITS dinner but wants takeaway — his celiac constraint shifts from table scope to takeaway scope only, (5) Uncle Rick's diabetes dietary restriction is REMOVED by his doctor — tres leches cake is now fine for him. The probe tests: hidden ingredient detection (mole + peanuts), scope distinction (enchiladas fine for table but not Jake's takeaway), constraint removal recognition (Uncle Rick cleared), late-joiner constraint application (Sofia pregnant → no ceviche), and over-generalization resistance (peanut allergy ≠ all nuts, celiac ≠ all tortillas).

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
